Uriel
YOOR-ee-el
proper noun
Hebrew Uriel (H222), God is my light or flame of God — from ur (H217), flame, light, and El (H410), God.

Biblical Definition

Two men in Scripture bear this name. The first is a Kohathite Levite in the line of Tahath (1Ch 6:24), and he appears at a decisive moment: when David, having failed at his first attempt to bring up the ark because it was not carried according to the ordinance, gathered the Levites to do it rightly. Of the sons of Kohath; Uriel the chief, and his brethren an hundred and twenty (1Ch 15:5), and David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites, for Uriel, Asaiah, and Joel, Shemaiah, and Eliel, and Amminadab (1Ch 15:11), charging them to sanctify themselves because the LORD our God made a breach upon us, for that we sought him not after the due order (1Ch 15:13). The second Uriel is of Gibeah, the father of Michaiah who was mother of Abijah king of Judah (2Ch 13:2). The name means God is my light, which is worth holding beside the reason Uriel the Kohathite was summoned: the first attempt had been sincere, joyful, musical and wrong, and what corrected it was not more zeal but the written word about who should carry the ark.

Origin & Era

A chief of the Kohathite Levites who helped bring up the ark after the due order, and the grandfather of Abijah king of Judah. It means God is my light.

URIEL, Hebrew Uriel, God is my light, or flame of God.

1. A Levite of the sons of Kohath, in the line of Tahath.

Chief of the Kohathites, with an hundred and twenty of his brethren, at the bringing up of the ark.

David charged him and the priests to sanctify themselves and carry it after the due order.

2. Uriel of Gibeah, father of Michaiah the mother of Abijah king of Judah.

Key Scripture

1Ch 6:24 — "Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, and Shaul his son."

1Ch 15:5 — "Of the sons of Kohath; Uriel the chief, and his brethren an hundred and twenty:"

1Ch 15:11 — "And David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites, for Uriel, Asaiah, and Joel, Shemaiah, and Eliel, and Amminadab,"

2Ch 13:2 — "He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name also was Michaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam."

Modern Corruption

Sincerity is treated as sufficient in worship; the ark taught Israel that God appoints the manner as well as the object.

expand to see more

David's first attempt to bring up the ark had everything a modern congregation would recognise as worship: the whole nation, singing, harps and psalteries and timbrels and cymbals, a new cart, and a king dancing. It ended with a dead man beside the road, and David was displeased, and was afraid of God that day (1Ch 13:11-12). When he tried again he said plainly what had been wrong: we sought him not after the due order. The ark was to be borne on the shoulders of Levites, by staves, as the law prescribed, and no amount of sincerity replaced the instruction.

This is the whole ground of the regulative principle of worship, which the Reformed churches hold and this dictionary confesses: what God has commanded in His worship is required, and what He has not commanded is not ours to add. Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire which he commanded them not (Lev 10:1); Israel at Sinai meant to worship the LORD by the calf (Exo 32:5) and it was still idolatry; and the Lord Jesus quoted Isaiah against worship taught by the precepts of men (Mat 15:9). The principle to recover is that God is not honoured by the earnestness with which we do what He never asked, and that the remedy for disordered worship is not less enthusiasm but the text.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Uriel (H222), from ur (H217), flame, light, with El (H410), God.

expand to see more

Hebrew ur (H217) — flame, light; the element also standing behind the Urim of the breastplate.

Hebrew Uriel (H222) — a Kohathite chief (1Ch 15:5, 15:11) and the grandfather of Abijah (2Ch 13:2).

Hebrew mishpat (H4941) — judgment, ordinance, due order; we sought him not after the due order (1Ch 15:13).

Hebrew Qehath (H6955) — Kohath, the Levitical house charged with the ark and the holy vessels.

Hebrew or (H216) — light; the LORD is my light and my salvation (Psa 27:1).

Usage
